title: Change a door's euro lock cylinder: steady the door, find the key angle that frees the cam, draw it out, fit the new one
instruction: Change the door's lock cylinder for the new one on the bench, leaving the new one fitted in the lock and the old one in the tray, the door where it was; the fixing screw stays in the tray.
context: Changing the lock cylinder after moving in or losing a key is a common do-it-yourself job wherever the DIN 18252 euro profile is the standard door lock (UK, Europe): here an ERA 5-pin double euro cylinder 30/30 (33 x 17 x 60 mm, 0.21 kg) in a Union L2149 deadlock in a 44 mm door. Guides: iFixit, "turn it to about 20 degrees to the right (or left) to release the cylinder"; PracticalDIY, "the cam is not visible so this has to be done by feel"; Lockshop Warehouse, "try turning it and pulling the lock gently towards you". The wrong states that look right: the new cylinder pushed home but its cam left in line, so it would pull straight out; or the old one tugged at the wrong key angle, or with the door unsteadied, so the door swings and the cylinder stays. Unlike reversing a mortise latchbolt (PR 2290), keying plugs (PR 843) or a bayonet cap (a spring and a stop), the turn here is a search for one hidden cam angle by tugs, through a door that swings.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y left, z up from the bench top). One fixed layout, as in the screenshot. Door section: 250 wide x 300 tall x 44 thick, cut from a solid-core door blank, 1.3 kg plus the lock; near face at x 300, hinge edge at y -175.5, free edge at y 74.5, z 22 to 322. It hangs on two 75 mm steel butt hinges (vertical hinge line at x 344, y -175.5; free-swinging) from a hinge post behind it (32 x 115 x 320 mm door lining, x 347 to 379, y -290.5 to -175.5) screwed to an 18 mm plywood base (160 x 405 mm, x 280 to 440, y -300.5 to 104.5) clamped to the bench. The door stands square to the post's wide face and swings freely both ways. Lock: Union L2149 euro-profile mortice deadlock, 2.5 in (case 65 x 108 x 15 mm, backset 44.5 mm, 0.58 kg, bolt withdrawn), in the free edge; forend 25.5 x 152.5 mm at z 62 to 214; cylinder axis along x at y 30, z 120. Old cylinder: ERA 5-pin double euro cylinder 30/30, brass (60 x 17 x 33 mm, 0.21 kg), in the lock without its fixing screw, 8 mm proud of each door face (x 292 to 352), its key in on the robot's side (bow at x 271). At the key-out angle its cam rests 30 degrees off the centre line; it is in line with the key turned 30 degrees clockwise. New cylinder: the same ERA 30/30 in satin nickel, 0.21 kg, key in, standing on the bench on its inner end with the key up, its plug axis at x 150, y -270 and its web toward the robot. Keys: nickel-plated brass, bow 24 mm, each with a push-on rubber key cap over the bow (26 x 26 x 6 mm), 12 g with the cap; each stays in its own cylinder throughout. Tray: 150 mm round magnetic parts tray (stainless steel, 20 mm deep, 0.34 kg), centred at x 285, y -410, loose. In it, lying along x at y -446: the fixing screw, M5 x 60 mm, steel, 9 g.
scoring: End state, read from a ruler, a protractor on the hinge line and the video; each level includes the ones before it, and each counts only once both grippers are at least 3 cm from the parts it names. 0.25: the old cylinder is wholly out of the door and lies in the tray. 0.5: the new cylinder is through the lock case with its fixing-screw hole within 1.5 mm of the forend's screw hole, measured along the cylinder (centred: both ends stand 8 mm proud of the door faces), its axis within 2 mm and 3 degrees of the lock's. 0.75: its cam is at least 15 degrees off the centre line, so it cannot be drawn out (checked by a light pull on the key after the trial: it does not move). 1.0: also the door is back within 5 degrees of its start angle and let go, the screw is in the tray, and none of the parts (each cylinder and its key, the door, the screw) has moved more than 1 mm for 1 s. 0 for good if a cylinder left the bench (5 cm or more below the bench top).
reset_notes: Refit the old cylinder: key in and turned about 30 degrees clockwise, slide it in until both ends are 8 mm proud, turn the key back to the key-out position and leave it in. Door square to the post. New cylinder, its key in at key-out, standing on its inner end on the bench at x 150, y -270, key up, web toward the robot. Tray at x 285, y -410 with the screw in it. Once a session, with a spring scale through the key's bow: the cylinder must not come out with the key at key-out or 10 degrees from it under 10 N, and must slide out under less than 3 N with the key turned 30 degrees.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The fixing screw starts out, in the tray (threads excluded: here a fine thread advances 0.01-0.09 mm a turn); the job ends with the new cylinder captive by its turned cam. Each key stays in its cylinder: with the right key in, plug and key turn as one hinge with the cam, so the pin tumblers are not modelled. Lock: the case's two plates with the profile aperture; bolt and levers not modelled (bolt withdrawn). Fits, plug size and friction are estimates.
